name: NarrativeEngine v0.7.3
body:
## Summary

The Director could start a letter, visit or ambush using something it was never offered, so a hallucinated NPC could show up at your door. Every pick is now checked against the options offered for that specific beat. An invalid pick gets one retry; if that also fails, nothing fires until the next evaluation.

## Fixes

- A visit or letter could come from an NPC who was never a valid sender for it, for example a leveled guard, your current follower, or someone who was only eligible to write a letter. That happened when the Director named an NPC that wasn't on the list. Senders are now checked against the list offered for that exact beat.
- A letter or visit could go ahead without its intended topic when the Director named a memory the sender didn't have. The composer then quietly picked a topic itself. That pick is now rejected.
- An ambush that named an attacker group nobody had offered quietly fell back to the first eligible group. That pick is now rejected.

## For Developers

- A rejected Director pick logs its reason and the retry to the plugin log. When both attempts miss, the decision log records the failure.
- The Director's chosen action name is now sanitized before it is logged or recorded.

name: NarrativeEngine v0.7.2
body:
## Summary

A pacing and placement update: visits stop arriving back to back, beats repeat less often, and beats no longer fire in other realms or sealed-off places.

## What's New

### Visits

- After any NPC visit, no other visit can happen for 24 in-game hours. Until now only the same visitor was held back, so different NPCs could turn up one after another.
- The new `iVisitBeatCooldownGameHours` setting in `NarrativeEngine.ini` controls how long the pause lasts. Set it to 0 to turn the pause off.
- A visit that's called off before the visitor reaches you doesn't start the cooldown.

> **Note:** Existing saves load normally. On the first load of an older save the cooldown starts clear, so the next visit isn't held back.

### The Director

- The Director now waits 15 minutes before choosing the same kind of beat again, up from 5. The old window mostly ran out while the beat was still playing, so it rarely prevented a repeat.

## Fixes

- Beats no longer fire in places nobody could plausibly reach you. Previously Vigilants of Stendarr could ambush you in the Soul Cairn. The default location blacklist now covers the Soul Cairn and the Boneyard, Apocrypha, the Mind of Pelagius, the inside of Azura's Star, the Forgotten Vale, Darkfall Passage, Ancestor Glade, the Throat of the World summit and path, Giant's Grove, Japhet's Folly, Brinewater Grotto, Forebears' Holdout and all of Castle Volkihar. It also still covers Sovngarde. Fort Dawnguard is deliberately left off.

name: NarrativeEngine v0.7.1
body:
## Summary

A small workaround for a rare case where Skyrim's own courier stops making deliveries.

## Fixes

- If Skyrim's pending-delivery counter has been driven below zero by something outside NarrativeEngine, the vanilla courier stops being dispatched and letters sit undelivered. The plugin now raises that counter to match the letters actually waiting whenever it stages one.

## For Developers

- `CourierUtils` caches the vanilla courier item-count global beside the quest and container it already tracked, and exposes a staged-letter count and a floor-only repair, with mocked-engine coverage.

name: NarrativeEngine v0.7.0
body:
## Summary

NarrativeEngine v0.7.0 rebuilds how a visiting NPC reaches you — they now walk Skyrim's real roads, and the spot they appear in is chosen for cover rather than raw distance — and fixes the bug behind the "gossip isn't spreading" reports. It also raises the hard floor to SkyrimNet Beta 25 and drops support for anything older.

## What's New

### NPC Visits

- Visitors now travel along Skyrim's actual road network instead of a straight line from home; both road graphs ship enabled by default.
- The arrival spot is chosen by walking outward along the visitor's approach route and taking the first place far enough away and out of sight, instead of picking from a fixed distance band.
- Spots with cover are preferred outright over open ground, so a visitor appears behind a rock 6,000 units out rather than in the open at 5,000.
- Where nothing offers cover, a visitor now needs 5,000 units of open ground rather than 3,000 — far enough that a figure appearing is ambiguous even if you turn a moment later.
- Visitors can finally arrive inside walled cities like Whiterun and Windhelm, which previously offered the arrival search no ground it recognised as standable.
- The minimum arrival distance rises from 800 to 2,000 units, which is what stops a visitor appearing across the road from you.
- A stuck visitor can now hop along the road to get around an obstacle before falling back to walking the long way round.
- Eleven new arrival and approach-chain tunables in `NarrativeEngine.ini` cover the graph's spacing, its four terrain difficulties, the stuck-recovery hop limits and the cover proximity test; the file documents each one inline.

## Fixes

- Gossip could stop spreading altogether: every rumor that survived a save came back unable to advance, and because those dead rumors still held slots against the live-rumor cap, enough reloads filled it and the world stopped seeding new ones.
- Letters and visits could be built around things the sender had no way of knowing — a recent fight or a place you had just been — because the Director wrote their motive in prose from its own player-centric view. It now names one of the sender's own memories instead.
- A visitor chosen from further down the candidate list arrived with no memories at all, leaving the composer nothing specific to work from.
- With you upstairs in an inn, a visitor could be sent to a balcony door on the floor above instead of the front door at street level.
- Which door a visitor waited at was effectively a coin flip in 279 of 544 vanilla interiors; it is now the same door every time, preferring one the engine has not flagged as minimal-use.
- A visitor from Winterhold could arrive 2,003 units west of Nightgate Inn while their whole route lay 11,106 units east; an arrival candidate must now hang off the route it was reached from.
- Arriving inside Whiterun's gate, a visitor could appear 789 units away and be greeted 1.3 seconds later; the gate arrival now walks out until the distance floor is met.
- The cover check counted any obstacle anywhere along the sight line, so on a 10,000-unit ray a boulder 400 units in front of the arrival read as clear cover. The blocker must now sit within 512 units of the spot.
- A single dead-end stub of navmesh could hide every other road in the loaded area, leaving a visitor to cross country beside a perfectly good road.
- A dead or absent NPC could be picked to start a rumor they could never spread, which also spent LLM calls on evaluating it.

## For Developers

- New `SKSE/NarrativeEngine_VisitorTravel.log`, rotated five deep and on by default, records one tagged line per decision in a visitor's journey — both endpoints, the graph, every candidate and the number that rejected it, the winner and the escort's hops. Turn it off with `bVisitorTravelLogEnabled`.
- The gossip trace gains a whole-world STATE summary at session start and after every tick, so a co-save round trip that loses something is visible by diffing the two blocks, plus a NOTE closing every tick on all paths.
- The gossip trace's session line now accounts for all six conversation outcomes; `silent` was 28% of every conversation over a fifteen-day run and was being dropped from the total.
- Per-key-press hotkey tracing moved behind `bTraceKeyPresses` (default off); under `bTraceMode` alone it cost a log line per keystroke of ordinary play.
- SkyrimNet content now lives in one Beta 25 plugin folder in the source tree and deploys verbatim, replacing the build logic that mirrored every file to both the old and new layouts.
- Three new engine findings recorded — land height outside the loaded grid, standable ground inside walled cities, and fine-road hop spans — plus a visitor-travel verification runbook.

## Notes

> **SkyrimNet Beta 25 (0.25.0) or newer is now required.** Beta 25 reorganised how SkyrimNet discovers plugin content, and this release ships only the new layout. On Beta 24 or earlier SkyrimNet will not find NarrativeEngine's prompts or settings at all: the mod loads and the dashboard opens, but every LLM-driven beat fails on a prompt that was never found. There is no compatibility mode — update SkyrimNet, or stay on v0.6.1. When upgrading, let your mod manager replace the whole mod rather than merging into it, so the old content folders don't linger.

> **Rumors stuck on your save will clear themselves out.** If gossip had gone quiet, the rumors responsible are discarded on the next load rather than restored, which frees the live-rumor slots they were holding and lets the world seed again.

name: NarrativeEngine v0.6.1
body:
## Summary

A maintenance release on top of v0.6.0: visitors now reach you from inside walled cities and greet you indoors, letter and visit prompts see only what you and that NPC actually said to each other, and every dashboard tab says when its next thing happens and on which clock.

## What's New

### The Dashboard

- Every tab with a cadence now shows when the next thing happens: Director evaluations, beat dispatch cooldowns, the gossip schedule, letter delivery, and the visit approach, return-home and conclusion-poll deadlines.
- Each readout is labelled with the clock that governs it — real, unpaused, active play, or game time — because those four elapse at different rates, and a bare "120s" against two of them means two different waits.
- A cooldown that is switched off reads as an em dash rather than 0s, so "why has this not fired yet" gets the right answer instead of the wrong one.

> **Note:** The numbers do not tick while you watch them. Opening the dashboard pauses the game, which freezes three of the four clocks for as long as the panel is on screen; each panel's footer says so.

### Beat Senders

- New `sBlacklistedSenders` under `[Beats]` names NPCs who may never be chosen to write you a letter or pay you a visit. Semicolon-separated, empty by default.
- An entry matches either the NPC's editor ID or the name shown in game, ignoring case, and one list covers both beats at once — including the count of whether a beat has any candidates left to pick from.

> **Note:** The list is read when the game loads, so changing it needs a restart. Editor-ID matching only works with an editor-ID recovery mod installed (powerofthree's Tweaks or equivalent) — without one, use the in-game name, and note that a name shared by several NPCs excludes all of them.

### Letters and Visits

- The dialogue history shown to the LLM when it writes a letter or plans a visit is now strictly what passed between you and that NPC. Lines they said to a third party, lines you said to someone else in earshot, and ambient NPC chatter are all dropped before the prompt is built.

### Ambushes

- The narration recorded in the world's event log when an ambush begins no longer contains speech of any kind — no quoted lines, none attributed to anyone, and no paraphrased speech either. The attackers do their own talking once the fight starts.

## Fixes

- An NPC who lives inside a walled city will now travel to you when you are nowhere near it. Previously the visit was declined outright whenever no city gate was loaded, which meant most visits from Whiterun, Riften, Solitude, Markarth and Windhelm residents never happened at all.
- A visitor who arrives at your door and follows you inside now greets you. They used to trail you at arm's length until the approach timed out and sent them home unheard.

## For Developers

- Both composers now share one dialogue-shaping module instead of each carrying its own fetch, age filter and annotator, so the two can no longer disagree about what counts as relevant history.
- The dashboard's timing arithmetic lives in one place, so the inactive-versus-expired distinction and the zero clamp are each written and tested once rather than once per tab.
- The Director tick interval's in-code fallback now matches the shipped INI at 90 seconds; it had been left at a development value of 30.
- The INI now names the clock each beat-dispatch knob runs on: `iBeatCooldownSeconds` advances only during active play, where `iBeatRepetitionWindowSeconds` is wall-clock and keeps running through pause, combat and dialogue.
- A new engine-findings note records that city worldspaces share Tamriel's coordinate origin, with the measured gate gaps behind it — 26 to 792 units across five cities — and why the parent-use flags mislead.
- Engine-mock test coverage for the new dialogue filter, the arrival-point re-anchoring, the dashboard timers, the sender blacklist and the settings parser.

name: NarrativeEngine v0.6.0
body:
## Summary

NPC visits are rebuilt around Skyrim's road network: a visitor now arrives up the road they would actually have walked, comes in through a city gate when the player is in a walled city, and comes in through the door when the player is indoors. This release also adds optional in-game debug notices, SkyrimNet Beta 25 support, and a large automated test suite.

## What's New

### NPC Visits

- Visitors arrive from along the road between the player and the sender's home, instead of appearing on a bearing with no relation to how they would have travelled.
- A visitor whose home lies outside a walled city now walks in through that city's gate — the nearest one to the player when the city has several.
- When the player is indoors, the visitor is placed on the far side of the player's own door and comes in through it, rather than the beat declining because nothing outdoors can be checked from inside.
- Senders who are not currently loaded — which is almost all of them — are now located from their save cell or the map marker of the location they are filed under.
- The arrival band widened from 2500 to 5000 units and the approach timeout from 60 to 90 seconds, together: the old ceiling was discarding roughly 70% of the road on a route before cover was even considered.
- A point with no cover is now accepted when it is far out and outside the player's view arc, because cover was only ever standing in for "nobody is watching this happen".
- The cover check sweeps a whole visitor's height rather than stopping at the chest, so an Altmer's head no longer shows over a rock that passed the test.
- A visitor whose walk stalls is escorted along the remaining fallbacks, gives up on positions that keep landing at the same dead end, and is always sent home when the visit ends.
- Three new tunables are live: `iVisitArrivalCoverRadiusUnits`, `bVisitArrivalAllowCoarseBearing`, and `iVisitMarkerMin`/`MaxDistanceUnits`, which were parsed but ignored until now.

> **Note:** One known limit — past roughly 2000 units an arrival can be accepted on a cover claim the raycast cannot really support, so a visitor may occasionally appear in plain sight. Observed once, at Falkreath.

### Debug Notifications

- An optional corner-of-the-screen notice when a beat does something you would otherwise miss entirely: an NPC warped in and walking over, a letter handed to the courier, an ambush spawned nearby, a rumor seeded.
- Off by default, and toggleable three ways: `bDebugNotifications` in the plugin INI, the MCM override, or a checkbox on the dashboard's Settings tab.

> **Note:** This is a testing aid, not a gameplay feature — the notices tell you things your character has no way of knowing. Leave it off for normal play.

### SkyrimNet Beta 25

- Prompts and the settings schema now deploy in Beta 25's plugin layout as well as the older one, so NarrativeEngine works on either side of the Beta 25 change with no action from you.

### Logs

- The main plugin log keeps the last five sessions instead of being wiped at every startup, so the log from the run where something went wrong survives the next launch.
- The event-history trace now ships on by default, so it is already recording when something odd turns up.
- The startup line names the build version, which makes a log tell you which release produced it.

## Fixes

- The dashboard hotkey matched mouse buttons as well as keys — the mouse reports wheel-down with the same ID code as the `8` key — so scrolling could open or close the dashboard. It now only matches keyboard events.
- A null field anywhere in an event payload threw away the whole batch of events after it. Malformed fields now fall back to a default and the rest of the batch renders.
- Log rotation renamed the current file, which detached any editor tailing it. It copies instead, so a tail stays attached across a rotation.
- The courier's cached lookup was not cleared when a save was loaded, so a reference resolved under one save could be handed out under the next.
- The MCM event sink traced every other mod's events, filling the log with hundreds of lines that had nothing to do with NarrativeEngine.

## For Developers

- A Catch2 test suite covering roughly 90 modules across two targets, one linking engine-free sources directly and one compiling production sources against real CommonLibSSE headers with a mock engine behind them. `build.ps1 test` builds both and runs ctest.
- The mock engine fabricates forms, cells, worldspaces, navmesh, references and vtables, which is what lets beats, arrival search, gossip and the dispatchers be tested without the game.
- `SenderCooldownTable` takes its clock and co-save as arguments rather than reaching for them, with `SKSECosaveIO` binding the port to SKSE.
- `_ne_VisitSenderFaction` and `_ne_SpawnMarkerTypeList` are gone from the plugin, along with the alias fill rules they fed; the visit quest's aliases are force-filled from C++ instead.
- CMake locates SkyrimNet's `CppAPI` headers in the separate devkit that Beta 25 splits them into, falling back to the older in-mod path.

name: NarrativeEngine v0.5.1
body:
## Summary

A repair release for the gossip system that shipped in v0.5.0. Gossip could not survive a save/load, and on many playthroughs never ticked at all. There is no new player-facing surface — this is fixes, diagnostics, and build hygiene.

## Fixes

- Gossip no longer loses everything on a save. Loading a game and then saving wiped the co-save record, so rumors, the ledger and the simulation clock were empty again every session; live state is now published at session start instead of over the staged record.
- Gossip's schedule survives a reload. The harvest interval restarted from zero on every load, so anyone whose sessions were shorter than one interval of unpaused play never saw a single sweep no matter how many in-game days they played; the schedule now resumes from the clock stored in the save.
- Returning to a save after a long gap runs one catch-up sweep stamped for the present, rather than one sweep per missed interval over the same memories.

## For Developers

- Gossip narrates its whole lifecycle to the plugin log — every load, save, publish, revert, and session start and end, each with a state fingerprint — so an idle gossip system reads differently from a broken one. These lines are not muted by `bGossipLogEnabled`.
- A sweep that examines zero memories now probes eight of the bucket's actors unfiltered, separating an empty SkyrimNet memory store from filters that reject every row, and names the offending filters when it is the latter.
- The beat pipeline accounts for every beat that never becomes a candidate: Ambush names which of its four refusals fired and how much cooldown is left, and the registry and dispatcher report beats dropped as disabled, polarity-mismatched, or recently fired.
- The build treats compiler warnings as errors by default (`NARRATIVEENGINE_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS` opts out) and the nine warnings already present are cleared; the CMake minimum rises to 3.24, below which that setting is silently ignored.
- Repo conventions are written down: commit-message format, where throwaway probe code goes, how test builds are named, and the structure of these release notes.

## Notes

- Requirements are unchanged from v0.5.0, but the README now states them. **SkyrimNet Beta 24 or higher** is a hard floor for gossip: it seeds through the filtered memory query that release introduced, and on anything older it refuses to run and says so in the log.
- **NPCs Have Relationships** remains a strongly recommended soft requirement. Gossip reads relationship records from your load order to decide who talks to whom, and vanilla authors very few, so without it rumors stay local far more often.

name: NarrativeEngine v0.5.0
body:
## The Gossip System

NarrativeEngine now runs a background social simulation: rumors that spread from NPC to NPC across Skyrim over in-world time.

Skyrim's unique NPCs are wired into a social graph built entirely from the game's own data — who shares a house, a town, a hold; who is related to whom; who belongs to the same organisation. When something notable happens to someone, it can become a rumor and start moving along that graph. The simulation runs regardless of where you are or what you are doing. It is not gated on loaded cells, and an NPC never has to be nearby to take part.

Who an NPC talks to is drawn by closeness — their household first, then their settlement, then their hold, and rarely anyone else in Skyrim. Factions and relationships move individuals along that ladder: a guild-mate three holds away or a sister in another city comes up far more often than a stranger would, while a rival or an enemy comes up less often than a neighbour. The Stormcloaks, the Imperial Legion, and the jarls' courts are how news crosses hold boundaries, because a garrison in every hold is the only province-spanning institution vanilla Skyrim actually has.

A rumor behaves like an infection. It stays interesting to whoever heard it for a few days, passes along with a chance per conversation set by how notable the original event was, and burns out when people keep telling it to those who already know.

Every telling writes memories — one on the teller, one on each listener. Those memories are the point: they are what SkyrimNet draws on when you talk to someone, so an NPC can know about something they were never present for, and know it because a specific person told them.

## Requirements

- **SkyrimNet Beta 24 or higher.** Gossip's seeding depends on the filtered memory query introduced in that release (plugin API v10). On an older SkyrimNet, gossip will not run and will report the version it found in the log — once, not every tick. The rest of NarrativeEngine is unaffected and works normally.
- **[NPCs Have Relationships](https://www.nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/mods/140482) — strongly recommended, but not required.** Gossip reads the relationship records in your load order to decide who talks to whom, and vanilla Skyrim authors very few of them. This mod fills that in, and needs no patch or configuration — the records are picked up automatically wherever they come from. Without it gossip still works, but the family and personal ties that carry a rumor beyond someone's own town are much thinner, so expect rumors to stay local more often.

## Actual Behavior

Gossip is slow, and that is deliberate. Set your expectations accordingly:

- **It has nothing to spread until NPCs have things worth spreading.** Rumors are seeded from NPCs' own memories of notable things that happened to them. On a new game those memory stores are nearly empty, so expect gossip to be rare to nonexistent early on.
- **It builds as you play.** The longer a save runs, the more memories NPCs accumulate, and the more material the simulation has to work with. A save with hundreds of hours on it will have noticeably more going on than a fresh one.
- **The pace is measured in in-game days, not minutes.** The simulation examines a slice of Skyrim's population every twelve in-game hours and seeds at most one new rumor per sweep, so any given NPC's turn to be examined comes around every few in-game days.
- **Most rumors stay local.** A typical rumor reaches a handful of people over a few days and dies out inside one settlement. Some cross into a neighbouring hold. Very few travel the province.
- **There is nothing to click.** Gossip surfaces in what NPCs say to you and to each other, not in a notification or a menu. The dashboard carries a tab tracking live rumors, but it is a diagnostic view rather than something you need to consult.

## Limited Impact

What gossip produces right now is NPC memories, and only that. As a rumor spreads, each NPC it reaches gains a memory of having heard about the event — who told them, and what they were told — and that memory feeds SkyrimNet's normal conversation context. An NPC may bring up something they were never present for, and know exactly who they heard it from.

Nothing else in the world reacts to a rumor yet. No NPC changes what they are doing because of one, no quest or beat fires from one, and no world state changes.

Memories are the foundation the rest of the system is being built on. Future background simulations will both feed gossip new material and react to what it has already spread.
